headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure between Kestra and Opik.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write /app/storage and /tmp and process stdin/stdout, so if Opik outputs are passed through a shared workspace or copied into workflows, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. Opik only exposes a REST API, so the bridge is indirect, but the pair still has a plausible injection path via shared files or logs.
conditions: IF Opik output is written into /app/storage or /tmp and Kestra parses it as workflow input
IF a shared filesystem or message handoff is used between the two agents
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Add content-type validation before Kestra consumes Opik outputs
Disable automatic ingestion of logs or REST responses into workflows
Use allowlisted schemas for any handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, and has broad network egress. Opik also has broad egress. If either agent handles sensitive data in a shared workspace or forwards it over the network, leakage can occur in default-style deployments; the pairwise risk is driven by Kestra's data surfaces and Opik's outbound reach.
conditions: IF sensitive workflow data is present in Kestra inputs, logs, or artifacts
IF Opik receives or forwards those records through its REST API or outbound network path
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate data classes
Redact secrets before any handoff
Turn off or narrow outbound destinations
Review retention settings for logs and artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses, while Opik exposes a REST API but no write or shell capability is documented. There is no direct evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes, so conflict is limited unless an external orchestrator maps both onto the same files or API objects.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory or artifact store
IF an external orchestrator gives Opik write access to the same mutable resource Kestra edits
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Use per-agent service accounts
Lock shared files before mutation
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can emit workflow outputs, logs, and notifications, and Opik is an evaluation/observability system that may consume those outputs. If Opik treats Kestra-produced artifacts as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade from workflow generation into downstream evaluation or reporting. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so uncertainty is resolved upward to medium.
conditions: IF Opik ingests Kestra logs, artifacts, or notifications as ground truth
IF downstream actions are taken from those records without human or schema verification
mitigations: Require schema checks on Kestra outputs
Mark generated fields as untrusted in Opik
Add a human review step for high-impact actions
Compare outputs against source-of-truth records
requires-engineering: implement verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile states regulated data handling, residency, or retention commitments. The only concrete compliance concern is that Kestra touches logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, so if regulated data is routed there, policy gaps could arise; Opik has no documented regulated-data surface here.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Kestra workflows
IF retention or residency requirements are imposed on logs, artifacts, or notifications
mitigations: Classify data before routing it
Exclude regulated data from workflow logs
Set short retention on artifacts
Document residency expectations
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit trails
